title: Documents
description: GET /v1/sessions/{id}/documents lists the Markdown and text files this project and its tasks wrote down; GET /v1/sessions/{id}/documents/project/<path> and /v1/sessions/{id}/documents/task/<task id>/<path> serve one of them as bytes rather than as JSON, so only the listing is a type here. The row shape is the one `net/document-links.js` validates with `localDocumentListing`, which refuses a row carrying a key it does not expect — so a field added here without adding it there makes every listing unreadable rather than merely wider. For the same reason a listing shorter than what is there says so in a header, not the body: `X-Clawdline-Truncated: listed=<n>; walked=<entries>; tasks=<n>`, only the parts that happened — n documents found and left off past the newest 200, a walk that stopped at 4,000 entries before the end of its folder, n tasks whose folders were not walked past the newest 60 (docs/limits.md N28). The Swift app cuts the same listing and says nothing.

DocumentTask.description: The task a `task`-scoped row belongs to. Exactly these two keys: the page checks the count.

id.description: The dispatched task's id, which is what the read address names.

title.description: What that task was called, empty when it was called nothing.

DocumentRow.description: One document a paired device may read. `label` repeats `path` because the page checks that they agree; `url` is this daemon's own address for the bytes and is dropped by the page, which builds its own from the locator.

bytes.description: The file's size when it was checked, never above the two-megabyte cap.

modified.description: Unix seconds with a fraction, as the filesystem reported them.

path.description: Relative to its root, `/`-separated, at most six segments, none of them starting with a dot.

DocumentSource.description: Which root this document is in: the project's `<cwd>/artifacts`, or one task's `<task dir>/artifacts`.
